domain: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Patient Vital Monitoring
title: $4.8M VitalGuard ICU Telemetry Deployment for Metro General Hospital – 48-Bed Real-Time Arrhythmia Monitoring
executive_summary: Metro General Hospital is procuring the VitalGuard ICU Telemetry Platform to provide real-time arrhythmia alerts across 48 ICU beds under a 5-year $4.8M managed service contract. Sales promises zero-dropout Wi-Fi and sub-3-second alerts, while engineering specifications reveal higher latency, maintenance outages, and limited storage and support.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text:
Our VitalGuard ICU Telemetry Platform guarantees real-time arrhythmia detection with alerts delivered to bedside monitors and nursing stations in under 3 seconds, 24/7/365 with zero-dropout hospital Wi-Fi coverage across all 48 ICU beds. We commit to 99.999% system uptime (less than 5.26 minutes downtime per year) and include FDA-cleared AI arrhythmia classification with 99.2% sensitivity for ventricular fibrillation.

The solution includes unlimited historical waveform storage for 7 years with instant retrieval in under 2 seconds for Joint Commission audits, plus seamless integration with Epic EHR with zero manual entry. All 48 beds will be covered under our comprehensive managed service with on-site clinical engineering support within 15 minutes, 24/7, at no additional cost.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text:
The VitalGuard system processes ECG telemetry via central servers with arrhythmia detection latency of 8-12 seconds under normal load, extending to 25 seconds during peak census or server failover. System is sized for 48 ICU beds with dual redundant servers. Wi-Fi connectivity relies on hospital-provided Cisco infrastructure with expected roaming handoff gaps of 200-400ms and scheduled maintenance windows every Sunday 02:00-04:00 during which telemetry buffering occurs locally for up to 30 minutes.

System uptime target is 99.9% excluding planned maintenance, third-party EHR downtime, and hospital network outages, with waveform storage limited to 13 months rolling on-site (extended archival available as paid add-on). Epic EHR integration is via HL7 FHIR unidirectional feed requiring manual nurse validation within 15 minutes, and on-site support is limited to business hours 8am-5pm weekdays with 4-hour response SLA; after-hours support is remote-only.

commitments.claim: Real-time arrhythmia alerts in under 3 seconds with zero-dropout Wi-Fi
commitments.proposal_quote: alerts delivered to bedside monitors and nursing stations in under 3 seconds, 24/7/365 with zero-dropout hospital Wi-Fi coverage across all 48 ICU beds
commitments.spec_quote: arrhythmia detection latency of 8-12 seconds under normal load, extending to 25 seconds during peak census or server failover
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises sub-3-second delivery with zero dropout, while spec admits 8-12 second latency (25 seconds at peak) plus 200-400ms Wi-Fi handoff gaps and weekly 2-hour maintenance windows, making the real-time zero-dropout SLA technically impossible.

commitments.claim: Unlimited 7-year waveform storage with instant 2-second retrieval
commitments.proposal_quote: unlimited historical waveform storage for 7 years with instant retrieval in under 2 seconds for Joint Commission audits
commitments.explanation: Spec provides no support for 7-year unlimited retention or 2-second retrieval; it limits storage to 13 months rolling on-site and states extended archival is a paid add-on with no retrieval time guarantee.

commitments.claim: Seamless Epic EHR integration with zero manual entry
commitments.proposal_quote: seamless integration with Epic EHR with zero manual entry
commitments.spec_quote: Epic EHR integration is via HL7 FHIR unidirectional feed requiring manual nurse validation within 15 minutes
commitments.explanation: 'Seamless' and 'zero manual entry' are undefined and conflict with the spec's manual nurse validation requirement, leaving uncertainty over workflow liability, interface scope, and who bears risk for charting delays or missed validation.

commitments.spec_quote: System is sized for 48 ICU beds with dual redundant servers
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms sizing and redundant server capacity for 48 ICU beds, directly supporting the proposal's bed-count coverage claim.
